plain: Catalina, an island off the coast of Southern California, is said by many to be a hotspot for UFOs that move between air and water. Michels brings this up more than once, crediting a book called Undersea UFO Base by a writer named Preston Dennett, and he says Catalina "might be the world's biggest hotspot of transmedium water-based UFOs," meaning objects that pass between sky and sea. He adds that a scientist named Townsend Brown spent the end of his life there. Separately, a retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet, arguing that the oceans are full of such objects, names the Catalina Channel itself as "a hot spot," without crediting Dennett. If true, it would mean these objects favour one stretch of water close to a major American coastline.
